phrases.text: So welcome back again.
Time for one more problem.
Now in this problem,
we are given that
two bikes
start from the same point.
The speed of bike A is twenty-eight kilometers per hour.
The speed of bike B is thirty-two kilometers per hour.
Both bikes are moving in opposite directions also. They keep moving for two hours.
The question is asking us to find how far apart they will be after two hours. Now let us assume the distance traveled by bike A is X kilometers,
and let the distance traveled by bike B be Y kilometers.
Now first,
let us understand one important concept.
The bikes are moving in opposite directions.
Because both bikes are moving away from each other,
the distance between them keeps increasing.
So the distance between the two bikes
will be the sum of their individual distances from the starting point.
That means
distance between the two bikes is equal to
X plus
Y.
Now let us find the distance traveled by each bike.
We know the formula,
distance is equal to speed into time.
For bike A,
X,
which is the distance traveled by bike A,
is equal to speed into time.
That is,
X is equal to
twenty-eight into two.
So
X is equal to fifty-six kilometers.
Now let us find the distance traveled by bike B.
Again,
using the same formula,
Y, which is the distance traveled by bike B, is equal to speed into time.
That is,
Y is equal to thirty-two into two.
After solving this,
Y is equal to sixty-four kilometers.
Now we know both distances.
So the distance between the two bikes is equal to X plus Y.
Putting the values,
distance is equal to fifty-six plus
sixty-four.
This gives us one hundred twenty kilometers.
So after two hours,
the two bikes will be one hundred twenty kilometers apart.
Hence,
the correct answer is option B
